pointers.sentence: `get_template_tag_modules` searches `django.templatetags` first, so these libraries can be loaded in every project, unless an application's module or the `"libraries"` option takes the same name ([Libraries: `Library`, custom tags and `{% load %}`](libraries.md)) (`django/template/backends/django.py:get_template_tag_modules`).

The language and the time zone are not in the context: each is held per thread, or per task in asynchronous code, as activated (`LocaleMiddleware`, where installed, activates the request's language; Django has no such middleware for the time zone) or else the default of `LANGUAGE_CODE` or `TIME_ZONE` (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:_active`, `django/utils/timezone.py:_active`, `django/middleware/locale.py:LocaleMiddleware.process_request`).

`StaticNode.handle_token` compiles the path as a filter expression, so it may be a variable, and takes a final `"as"` and a name as a variable to set in place of printing (`django/templatetags/static.py:StaticNode.handle_token`).
`StaticNode.render` escapes it when autoescaping is on (`django/templatetags/static.py:StaticNode.handle_simple`, `django/templatetags/static.py:StaticNode.render`).
`StaticNode.render` escapes it when autoescaping is on (`django/templatetags/static.py:StaticNode.handle_simple`, `django/templatetags/static.py:StaticNode.render`).
The function `static` gives Python code the same lookup (`django/templatetags/static.py:static`).

The storage may name another file: `ManifestStaticFilesStorage`, with `settings.DEBUG` off, uses the hashed name its manifest records, and by default raises `ValueError` mid-render for a path the manifest lacks (`django/contrib/staticfiles/storage.py:ManifestFilesMixin.stored_name`; [Static file storages: `ManifestStaticFilesStorage` and hashed names](../contrib/static-storage.md)).
`{% get_static_prefix %}` and `{% get_media_prefix %}` print `STATIC_URL` and `MEDIA_URL`, read from the settings, without the storage or escaping (`django/templatetags/static.py:PrefixNode.render`).
`{% translate %}`, or `{% trans %}`, takes a string or a variable, with filters, and the options `"noop"`, `"context"` and `"as"` (`django/templatetags/i18n.py:do_translate`).

At each render its node marks the `Variable` in its filter expression for translation, unless `"noop"` was given, and `Variable.resolve` then returns a lazy translation, by `django.utils.translation.gettext_lazy`, or `django.utils.translation.pgettext_lazy` with a context (`django/template/base.py:Variable.resolve`).
`render_value_in_context` makes it a string, in the language active then, and escapes it as any value (`django/templatetags/i18n.py:TranslateNode.render`).

A literal in a template is safe, and translation keeps a safe message safe, so `{% translate "Ships" %}` prints the translation's tags as tags, while `{% translate name %}`, holding the same string, escapes them (`django/utils/translation/trans_real.py:gettext`, [Autoescaping and safe strings](autoescape.md)).
Anything else there, a comment included, is an error (`django/templatetags/i18n.py:do_block_translate`).
It fills each placeholder by looking its name up in the context as one key, and renders the value with `render_value_in_context` (`django/templatetags/i18n.py:BlockTranslateNode.render`).

`{% language "de" %}` renders its body inside `django.utils.translation.override`, which activates German and afterwards restores the previous language (`django/templatetags/i18n.py:LanguageNode.render`).
Translations in the body follow it, and so do number and date formats, which `django.utils.formats` takes from the active language (`django/utils/formats.py:get_format`).

`{% get_current_language %}`, `{% get_current_language_bidi %}` and `{% get_available_languages %}` read the active language as their node renders, the last giving `LANGUAGES` with each name translated into it; `{% get_language_info %}`, `{% get_language_info_list %}` and filters such as `|language_name_local` look a code up in Django's table of languages (`django/utils/translation/__init__.py:get_language_info`).

Not so the context processor `django.template.context_processors.i18n`: its `"LANGUAGE_CODE"` is computed when the template is bound to its `RequestContext` (`django/template/context_processors.py:i18n`).

`render_value_in_context` formats numbers, dates and times with `django.utils.formats.localize`, passing `Context.use_l10n`, by default `None`, which means localise (`django/template/base.py:render_value_in_context`, `django/utils/formats.py:localize`).

`render_value_in_context` formats numbers, dates and times with `django.utils.formats.localize`, passing `Context.use_l10n`, by default `None`, which means localise (`django/template/base.py:render_value_in_context`, `django/utils/formats.py:localize`).
`{% localize off %}` sets the flag for its body and restores it after; `{% localize %}` or `{% localize on %}` sets it true (`django/templatetags/l10n.py:LocalizeNode.render`).

Before it localises, `render_value_in_context` converts an aware datetime to the current time zone when `Context.use_tz` is true or, while it is `None`, when `USE_TZ` is; a filter registered with `expects_localtime=True`, as `date` is, gets its value converted first (`django/utils/timezone.py:template_localtime`, `django/template/base.py:FilterExpression.resolve`).

`{% localtime off %}` sets `use_tz` for its body as `{% localize %}` sets `use_l10n` (`django/templatetags/tz.py:LocalTimeNode.render`).

`{% timezone "Europe/Malta" %}` changes which zone is current, rendering its body inside `django.utils.timezone.override`, and `{% get_current_timezone as TIME_ZONE %}` names it (`django/templatetags/tz.py:TimezoneNode.render`, `django/templatetags/tz.py:GetCurrentTimezoneNode.render`).

`{% timezone "Europe/Malta" %}` changes which zone is current, rendering its body inside `django.utils.timezone.override`, and `{% get_current_timezone as TIME_ZONE %}` names it (`django/templatetags/tz.py:TimezoneNode.render`, `django/templatetags/tz.py:GetCurrentTimezoneNode.render`).

A `datetime.datetime` takes no new attributes, so `do_timezone` copies its result into `datetimeobject`, a subclass that exists to carry a flag telling `template_localtime` to leave it alone (`django/templatetags/tz.py:do_timezone`).

`do_cache` parses the body into a node list and reads a timeout, a fragment name, any values to vary on and an optional last `using=` naming a cache, compiling all but the name as filter expressions (`django/templatetags/cache.py:do_cache`).
On a hit the body is not rendered; on a miss it is rendered and stored (`django/templatetags/cache.py:CacheNode.render`, `django/core/cache/utils.py:make_template_fragment_key`).
